newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH INDMIN SUGGESTS GOVT RESIGNATION.
newsitem.headline: CZECH INDMIN SUGGESTS GOVT RESIGNATION.

text.p: Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy suggested on Friday that the current cabinet should resign and a new one, from the same coalition parties, be formed in its place to resolve current political problems.

A spokesman for Dlouhy's party, the neo-liberal Civic Democratic Alliance, said the remarks represented "at this point" Dlouhy's private view, but added the party would debate the minister's idea soon.
"The resolution of the current situation could be the resignation of the cabinet and the creation of a new one within the current coalition," spokesman David Rozanek quoted Dlouhy as saying.
The government has been facing growing public distrust as economic growth, the cornerstone of its policies, has slowed since the beginning of this year.

A worsening foreign trade balance, rapid erosion of the exchange rate of the crown and a number of economic crime scandals has led to a loss of confidence from both Czech public and foreign investors.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, head of the senior partner in the three-party coalition, the Civic Democratic Party (ODS), rejected Dlouhy's idea.
"If Dlouhy made a decision concernig himself... he should not pass it to others," CTK news agency quoted him as saying.
Dlouhy has said he is considering leaving the cabinet by the end of this year and other members of the cabinet have said the government could be restructured later this summer.
Dlouhy and Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik of ODS have been under heavy fire for failing to regulate financial markets, keep the state budget in balance and curb the trade gap.
Opinion polls have shown a steady decline of confidence in the government, and a large drop in the ODS's ratings, triggering debate within the party on replacing its leaders.
